beats.say: I am Xerath. Magus Ascendant. I have transcended flesh, death, and the concept of a dash.
And this is Kurbo. Kurbo also plays Xerath. Kurbo presses Q, and then simply never lets go.
I was charging it for maximum power!
While you hold it, I am slowed. I become a very expensive sarcophagus, standing in the open, waiting for a hook.
Here's the rule. Arcanopulse grows from seven fifty to fourteen fifty range, over one and a half seconds. The charge is the range.
So don't charge to full. Charge to them. The instant the end of the line is past the target, let go.
And it lands half a second after you release. They are walking, Kurbo. Aim where they will be, not where they were.
Bad Kurbo: full charge, aimed at their feet, misses, slowed the whole time. Good Kurbo: short charge, led, hits. Same button.
Go to APEX. Practice. Xerath. Arcanopulse. Do it until your fingers let go on their own. Ascend.
My Eye sees the future. Kurbo sees the present. Barely. On a good day.
Eye of Destruction lands three quarters of a second after you press it. In that time, a champion walks about two hundred and fifty units.
So I just put it on them, right?
No. If you put it on them, they walk out of the middle, and the middle is the whole point.
The centre deals two thirds more damage, and slows by sixty percent. The edge is a love tap. The centre is a sentence.
Look where they are walking. Put the centre a step ahead of them, and let them walk into it.
Bonus: a centred Eye slows them so hard that the Arcanopulse after it basically aims itself.
APEX. Practice. Xerath. Eye of Destruction. The future awaits, and it is slightly to the left of where they are standing.
Shocking Orb is a missile. It stops on the first thing it touches, and it stuns for longer the farther it flew.
Point blank, three quarters of a second. At full range, two and a quarter. Three times the stun, for the crime of pressing E sooner.
Kurbo waits until the assassin is in his lap, then throws the orb.
That is not an orb. That is a hug. A short, disappointing hug.
Throw it the moment they start coming. Long flight, long stun, and you are still far away when it lands.
Why did my orb hit a minion?
Because minions block it. Look at the line first. Step to the side for a clear lane, or wait for the gap.
APEX. Practice. Xerath. Shocking Orb, and then The Retreat. Make them sleep far, far away.
I have no dash. I have never had a dash. My escape is being somewhere else, beforehand.
This is the most important video. Every enemy has a threat range: how far they can walk and dash onto you before you react. Draw it in your head, in red.
Your Arcanopulse reaches fourteen fifty. Draw that around them, in blue. The ring of floor between red and blue is the band.
In the band, I hit them, and they cannot touch me. Outside it, I am useless. Inside red, I am dead.
But I need to be close to hit my Eye!
Then you don't throw the Eye. Your Eye reaches a thousand, which is inside a lot of red rings. Only use it on someone who can't reach you.
And remember, charging slows you. So charge while walking backwards, and let go early. Never stand still inside their ring holding Q.
When they commit, back off. When they settle, step back up to range. You are not running away. You are keeping a distance.
In lane it is the same. Stand behind your wave, outside their range, and poke over the minions. The band is everywhere.
APEX. Practice. Xerath. The Band. Live there. Pay rent there. Die of old age there.
Good players dodge. They see your Eye, they walk out. They see your Q telegraph, they step aside.
Throwing my Arcanopulse at a healthy Ezreal is not an attack. It is a light show, for his enjoyment.
But a stunned target can't dodge anything. So: orb first. Then, while they are stunned, Eye on their feet, and the pulse through them.
Can I do Q first?
No. Charging Q locks out your E and your W. Orb, Eye, then pulse. In that order, every time.
The orb is the question. The Eye and the pulse are the answer. Do not answer before the question has been asked.
APEX. Practice. Xerath. Stun, Then Everything. Waste nothing.
My ultimate. I root myself, and rain judgement across the map. Four shots, each landing six tenths of a second after I call it.
So I fire all four really fast at them!
All four at the same spot means one guess, four times. They juke once, and you miss all of it.
Fire one. Watch which way they dodge. Put the next one where the dodge is going. Every shot is a different guess.
And I am rooted. So before I begin, I make sure nobody is close enough to interrupt my sermon.
So that's it, Kurbo. Let go of Q. Lead the Eye. Orb early. Live in the band. Stun, then everything.
APEX. Practice. Xerath. Start at stage one. Finish at Magus Ascendant. Kurbo, ascend.
